 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Sambasiva Rao Naidu

Court-cum-Motor Vehicles Accidents Claims Tribunal, Hyderabad dated 09.10.2019 by which the
learned Tribun

sentences.text:
al allowed the petition filed by the respondent/claimant and awarded a sum of Rs.23,40,000/- together with costs and interest, the respondent Nos.2 and 3 i.e., Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TSRTC) represented by its Managing Director, preferred this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act., on the following grounds:
The judgment and decree of the Tribunal is contrary to law, against the facts of the case.

The Tribunal committed an error in awarding a sum of Rs.23,00,400/- with costs and interest as against the claim of respondents for Rs.60,00,000/- on account of death of deceased Vikas Kumar Jain in a road traffic accident dated 19.03.2017.

The appellants have claimed that the Tribunal committed irregularity in holding that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the RTC bus without any acceptable evidence on record.

The appellants have claimed that the Tribunal ought to have appreciated and verified whether there is contributory negligence on the part of rider of the motor bike on which the deceased was travelling as pillion rider at the time of accident.

The Tribunal failed to consider the fact that the claimant did not make the owner and insurer of the motor bike which involved in the accident as parties to the claim petition, thereby the petition ought to have been dismissed on the ground of non-joinder of necessary parties.
The Tribunal committed an error by accepting the evidence of PW2.
Since he is none other than the rider of the motor bike which involved in the accident and his evidence cannot be relied to prove the accident.

The Tribunal failed to appreciate the fact that there was no independent eye witness to prove the contents of Ex.P2 (charge sheet) thereby, the Tribunal ought not to have relied on Ex.A2 for awarding compensation against the appellants herein.

2. The appellants have claimed that since the application was filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act., the respondents/claimants are suppose to prove the negligence on the part of driver of the bus and in case of their failure, the Tribunal ought to have drawn an adverse inference that the accident occurred due to negligence of rider of the motor bike.
The appellants have claimed that the finding of the Tribunal about the income of the deceased as Rs.1,44,000/- per month without any income certificate is incorrect and liable to be set aside.

The Court below relied on Ex.A7 The Telangana State Road Transport ... vs Mamta Jain And 3 Others on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113128239/
1 income tax returns to show that the deceased was having income from house property.

sentences.text: But, according to the appellants, the same cannot be taken as income of the deceased.
The appellants have claimed that the Tribunal committed an error by considering a sum of 40% of the future prospects, even though the income of the deceased is not established.

While questioning the amounts awarded under the other heads, the appellants have contended that the Tribunal ought not to have awarded the interest @ 9% per annum and in view of the settled proposition of law, the Tribunal ought not to have awarded a sum of Rs.23,00,400/-, thereby they sought for setting aside the order.

3. Before going to the merits of the appeal, a glance on the record would indicate that M.V.O.P.No.559 of 2018 has been filed by the respondent Nos.1 to 3 with a prayer for compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- on account of death of the deceased in a road traffic accident.

According to the record placed before the Tribunal, it was the case of respondents herein that on 19.03.2017 the deceased and his friend were proceeding from Narayanaguda to Liberty on motor bike and when they reached Gahana Jewellers, Himayathnagar, Hyderabad, the driver of the RTC bus bearing No.AP-11-Z-6335 which was also proceeding in the same direction, drove the bus in rash and negligent manner, dashed the two wheeler from the back side, due to which the deceased fell down, received severe injuries and died on the spot.
The rider of the bike also sustained injuries.
The respondents have filed the petition with a plea that the deceased was aged 32 years at the time of accident with good health.
He was earning Rs.30,000/- per month on his business.
The sudden death of the deceased put the petitioners to loss of life support, love and affection, thereby sought for a sum of Rs.60,00,000/-.
The 1st respondent/driver of the RTC bus remained exparte.
The appellants have contested the petition.

The Tribunal framed the following issues :
1. Whether the pleaded accident had occurred resulting in death of the deceased Vikas Kumar Jain @ Vikas Kumar Bhansali, due to rash and negligent driving of the RTC bearing registration No.AP-11A 6335, by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to any compensation, if so, at what quantum and what is the liability of the respondents?
3.

4. During enquiry, the respondents/claimants have examined PWs 1 and 2 and marked Exs.A1 to A8.
The appellants herein did not adduce any evidence.

5. After conclusion of the enquiry, and after hearing both parties, the Tribunal allowed the petition in part, directing the appellants herein to pay a sum of Rs.23,00,400/- under various heads together with costs and interest @ 9% per annum.

sentences.text: 6. Heard both parties.

7. Now the point for consideration is:
Whether the Tribunal failed to appreciate the evidence placed by both parties and came to wrong conclusion, thereby awarded excess compensation, if so, whether the award is liable to be set aside?
8. POINT:

The appellant/Telangana State Road Transport Corporation filed this appeal challenging the award whereunder the learned Chairman, Motor Vehicles Accident Claims Tribunal, Hyderabad awarded a sum of Rs.23,00,400/- towards compensation on account of death of deceased in a road traffic accident and the appeal is filed mainly on the ground that the Tribunal did not consider the contributory negligence on the part of rider of the motor bike on which the deceased was traveling at the time of accident.

sentences.text: The appellants have further claimed that the Tribunal committed an error by awarding compensation though the appellant did not add the insurer of the motor bike which involved in the accident.

Apart from those the appellants have find fault with the observations made by the Tribunal through which it considered the income of the deceased as Rs.1,44,000/- per month without filing any income proof.
The next contention of the appellant is with regard to considering 40% future prospects on the above referred income.
9. It is true as per the admitted case of respondents/appellants, the accident occurred when the deceased was going on a motorcycle of PW2 as its pillion rider.
The appellants did not choose to examine any witness on its behalf.
Absolutely there is no material before the Court to believe that there was contributory negligence on the part of PW2 in the above referred accident.

According to evidence of PW2 and as per the contents of the charge sheet filed before the Tribunal vide Ex.A2 it was the case of appellants that while the deceased and Pw2 were proceeding on motor bike, the driver of RTC bus bearing No.AP-11-Z-6335 which was driven in high speed and in rash and negligent manner, dashed the bike.
Noting was elicited from PW2 to establish such contributory negligence.
Similarly, the appellants did not produce any witness including the driver of the bus which involved in the accident to prove that there was contributory negligence by PW2.

Therefore,
in the absence of such evidence, it cannot be held that there was contributory negligence and appellant/s herein is not liable to pay compensation.
Therefore, the said ground cannot be considered.
10. The other contention of the appellant is with regard to the evidence of PW2 on the ground that he is an interested witness.
As per the evidence of PW2 he is none other than the rider of the bike on which the deceased was travelling and which involved in the accident when the above referred bus dashed the bike.

Therefore, PW2 is quite natural witness and the cross examination of PW2 will not The Telangana State Road Transport ... vs Mamta Jain And 3 Others on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113128239/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3 help the appellant to show that there is some interestedness on the part of PW2 to support the case of appellant.
11. The next contention of the appellants is that the Tribunal committed an error by considering the income of the deceased as Rs.1,44,000/- per month without any income proof.
In fact, as per the award, the Tribunal having considered the tax returns vide Ex.A7 for the assessment year 2015-2016, considered the annual income of the deceased as Rs.1,44,000/-.
The post mortem report which is marked as Ex.A4 shows the age of the deceased as 32 years.

Therefore, being young and able bodied person, it may not be difficult for such a person to earn Rs.12,000/- per month i.e.,
Rs.400/- per day.
Now a days, even a coolie on daily wage is able to earn income Rs.400/- to Rs.500/- per day.
The tax returns marked as Ex.A7 was filed for the year 2015-2016.
The accident occurred on 19.03.2017.
Therefore, it cannot be said that the above referred tax returns was prepared with a view to get more compensation in the present case.

As per the judgment in Pranay Sethi's case, the Hon'ble Apex Court was please to observe that in case of person without any permanent employment and if his age is less than 40 years a sum of 40% of the admitted income can be considered as further prospects, thereby the Tribunal rightly considered the income of the deceased as Rs.2,01,600/-, which includes Rs.1,44,000/- annual income and Rs.57,600/- i.e., 40%
of the above said income.
The Court below rightly deducted 1/3 of the said income towards his personal expenditure and arrived a sum of Rs.21,50,400/- as loss of dependency.
The other heads namely funeral expenses, loss of estate and consortium of wife and other petitioners is also as per the observations made in Pranay Sethi's case.
Therefore, the Tribunal awarded the above referred compensation by taking into all the circumstances including oral and documentary evidence.
Absolutely, there are no grounds to conclude that the said compensation is on higher side.

Therefore, there are no merits in the appeal and it is liable to be dismissed.
12.
In the result, the appeal is dismissed.
No costs.
As a sequel, pending Miscellaneous Applications, if any, shall stand closed.
